hidden_target.material_initial_state: A mixed powder consisting of ZrB2 ceramic powder (>99.8% purity, 1–5 μm) and 30% AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder prepared from equimolar Al, Fe, Ni, Co, and Cr powders by ball milling; the powders were ethanol-milled and vacuum-dried before sintering.
hidden_target.intervention: ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr cermets were consolidated by spark plasma sintering at 1300, 1400, 1500, or 1600 °C to determine the sintering temperature giving the best mechanical properties and resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion and wear.
hidden_target.conditions: SPS was performed under vacuum at 50 MPa, approximately 200 °C/min, with a 5 min hold. Corrosion specimens were immersed in molten Al at 700 °C for 4, 8, or 12 days. Ball-on-disc wear tests used a Si3N4 ball at room temperature, 10 N load, 500 r/min, and 30 min.
hidden_target.structural_mediator: At 1500 °C, the liquid high-entropy-alloy binder uniformly filled pores and strongly connected ZrB2 grains, producing the highest relative density (97.71%) and a compact microstructure. At 1600 °C, binder overflow/loss generated additional pores and reduced relative density to 94.73%.
hidden_target.mechanism: Increasing temperature through 1500 °C improves binder fluidity, pore filling, grain bonding, and densification, suppressing molten-Al penetration, ZrB2-grain detachment, and abrasive wear while improving hardness and crack resistance. Excessive temperature causes binder loss, poorer bonding, and porosity, allowing aluminum to enter through pores and cracks and corrode the metal binder into Al-rich reaction products.
hidden_target.predicted_outcome: Relative to cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C, the 1500 °C material should exhibit the greatest density, hardness, and fracture toughness, the lowest molten-Al corrosion rate and wear volume, and more stable friction behavior; its fracture toughness should also exceed that of pure ZrB2.
hidden_target.baseline: ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, and 1600 °C served as the principal processing baselines; pure ZrB2 ceramics (reported fracture toughness 4.5 MPa·m^1/2) were used as a toughness reference.
hidden_target.boundary: The optimum was observed for the tested 30%-binder ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr composition sintered at 1500 °C under the stated SPS schedule. Performance declined at 1600 °C because of binder overflow. Corrosion conclusions apply to molten Al at 700 °C for up to 12 days, and wear conclusions apply to the specified room-temperature ball-on-disc test.
hidden_target.discriminating_measurement: SEM/EDS and XRD characterized phases, pores, interfaces, and corrosion layers; Archimedes relative density, Vickers hardness/indentation fracture toughness, thickness-loss corrosion rate after molten-Al exposure, wear volume, and friction coefficient distinguished the four sintering conditions.
hidden_target.actual_result: The 1500 °C cermet gave the best overall performance: 97.71% relative density, 1911.8 HV hardness, and 6.79 MPa·m^1/2 fracture toughness (about 1.4 times pure ZrB2). After 12 days in molten Al, its reported average corrosion rate was 1.225 × 10^-3 mm/h, lower than 4.751 × 10^-3, 3.253 × 10^-3, and 2.593 × 10^-3 mm/h for the 1300, 1400, and 1600 °C samples, respectively. Its wear volume was the lowest at 0.104 mm^3, with a relatively stable average friction coefficient of 0.46. The conclusion instead states 1.225 × 10^-4 mm/h for corrosion, inconsistent with the abstract and detailed results.
